Marketing.problem: The only title option reads like a doc label. It starts with "Read", names no pain, and leaves out the "no code changes" promise that has worked for Abhi. It also omits the words an engineer would search: "db.client.operation.duration", "database metrics", "query latency". I would not put my name on it, and I can't pick a better option because none was offered.
Marketing.fix: Send back a title that credits the OTel Java agent and Splunk with the result. It should carry the reader's goal (Postgres query latency in Splunk, no app code changes, one env var) and a searchable term such as db.client.operation.duration or "database metrics". Keep the p95 promise worded to match what the proof shows.

Marketing.problem: The title promises a "p95" and the brief wants it "in milliseconds". With the default buckets, a 30 ms query sits in a wide bucket (roughly 10 to 50 ms). The interpolated p95 could land well off the 30 ms truth. known_query_p95_vs_truth_pct only has to be "present", so a large gap would still pass and break the title's promise.
Marketing.fix: Set a real acceptance rule for the p95 reading. For example, require the SignalFlow p95 to fall inside the stored bucket that contains the timer's p95. Also report the bucket edges next to the reading. If the gap is large, the title should say "bucket-accurate p95" or similar. It should not imply exact milliseconds.

Marketing.problem: The opening is likely to be built on the "before" measurement of zero series and on the one-bucket imprecision. That would frame the agent's default as missing something and put a cost at the top. The reader has to be able to take this as a positive gain, not as a flaw.
Marketing.fix: Open with what the reader gets: p95 query latency charts across Java services from one env var, with no code changes. Describe the zero-series run as the agent's opt-in default. Put bucket precision and the dup-name behaviour in the body as things to plan for.
